components: a short stroke slanting down to the right, whose end meets the long stroke
a long stroke that sweeps down to the left from the upper right, curves round and runs out to the right along the base
strokeOrder: draw the short stroke from its top down and to the right
lift, begin at the upper right and sweep down to the left past the end of the short stroke, then without lifting curve round and run out to the right along the base
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03068 file records と as two stroke paths in this order and direction: the short stroke, then the long sweep; so there is one pen lift.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03068.svg, hiragana と (U+3068 HIRAGANA LETTER TO), two stroke paths kvg:03068-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 starts at the top of the short stroke and runs down and to the right, ending on the line s2 will take; s2 starts at the upper right, sweeps down to the left, curves round and runs out to the right along the base. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. In KanjiVG and in the print glyph alike, the short stroke ends on the long one, so the two strokes touch.

notes: Fourth sign of ありがとう.
